# Local offline adaptation

Source: Kyutai Pocket TTS v4.0.1, commit `a922b912dfa366975294afb568d815b305acde5d` (MIT). Original file hashes are in `PINNED_SOURCES.txt`. The unmodified model YAML is embedded as a resource. All source changes are local to this directory. This component's original ABI and registry code is Apache 2.0 under the repository license. The adapted modules remain under Kyutai's MIT terms (`KYUTAI-MIT-LICENSE`). The `ptts` dependency is the exact `7efa26973f81bba42cf2ace8da2c1eb9b605d54d` fork of xn-ptts, with default features off; its license is MIT OR Apache 2.0.

`xn` is pinned to exact `0.2.12`, matching the verified Kyutai `rust/Cargo.lock` entry (full lockfile SHA-256 `3f2c5396eaaad4c64258ae724e012fdaa0c7b3e71165bcf0ef2c6b0641d18d27`). The earlier `0.2.11` pin came from the upstream semver manifest rather than the resolved lockfile. `tests/test_xn_pin.py` checks this alignment from a small checked-in lock-entry fixture; it does not compile the Rust component.

- `config.rs`: remove embedded language catalog, arbitrary configuration loading and dynamic source selection. The C ABI embeds only `english_18m_2026-10.yaml` and substitutes verified local paths into its bundle weights and tokenizer fields. Unused per-module `flow_lm.weights_path` and `mimi.weights_path` fields are omitted; the pinned YAML has neither. Its architecture and generation constants remain the publisher's.
- `model.rs`: remove voice-cloning/audio-file loading, predefined voice selection, voice export and the two-thread unbounded latent channel. The existing model math, prompt construction, EOS rules and first-frame fade remain; each latent is decoded and delivered synchronously. Cancellation is checked before expensive steps and before output. The generation ceiling is 375 frames/30 seconds.
- `tokenizer.rs`: retain SentencePiece only and reject its unknown piece ID and exact `<0xHH>` byte fallback pieces before generation; no JSON/Hugging Face tokenizer.
- `rng.rs`: retain the upstream fixed default seed and remove environment-controlled seed selection.
- `text.rs`: retains the upstream prompt preparation and punctuation rules; removes sentence splitting, decoding helpers and logging. `weights.rs`: retained with no functional changes; safetensors key mapping follows the pinned source.
- `lib.rs` and `include/sign_pocket_tts.h`: new bounded request registry, exact asset hash checks, C ABI, text checks, signed PCM conversion, callback cancellation and error status separation. No path, input text or audio is logged.

Asset layout for a caller-controlled *private, immutable* directory: `model.safetensors` (111,728,528 bytes), `tokenizer.model` (59,339 bytes), and `alba.safetensors` (4,163,992 bytes). Exact SHA-256 values are compiled into `lib.rs` and match `native/vendor/pocket-tts-audition/manifest.json`. The originals are Kyutai CC BY 4.0, and the Alba embedding is attributed to Alba MacKenna under CC BY 4.0. No model asset is copied into this source tree. The component accepts no runtime downloader, network URL, cloning source, or alternate model name.

`sts_pocket_create` does not load weights, allowing another thread to cancel a request during hash verification or load. Each synthesize call loads a private model instance; this deliberately avoids global model cache ownership until phone memory is profiled. The JNI owner must keep the PCM callback and userdata live for the synchronous call and must not unload the library until in-flight calls return. The component wipes its owned UTF-8 byte copy and PCM staging buffer, but makes no secure-erasure claim for upstream tensor allocations, borrowed JNI input or the model files. Source-only tests exercise registry ownership, cancellation, input validity and PCM callback bounds. A hosted full compile, unit suite and real-model component probe are required before admission; no build, model, device or key was used on the owner PC for this implementation.

## Test-first adapter-contract repairs

The hosted RED run [40330044633](https://github.com/Hatsunama/sign-to-speak/actions/runs/40330044633) compiled the pinned source at `43f9f96481853fb69809852440f906940c15f7b1` and ran 14 Rust unit tests: 10 passed and four failed. The four failures were empty PCM incorrectly returning `Ok`, finite out-of-range PCM being clamped, a nonfinite sample allowing an earlier part of its frame to reach the sink, and frame-limit exhaustion without post-EOS completion returning success. The local receipt is `C:/sign_to_speak/speech-native-integration-20261026/component-red-40330044633.log`.

The adapter now requires at least one PCM sample for successful completion, validates every sample and the duration budget for a full decoded frame before changing pending PCM or calling the sink, and reports a generation error unless the post-EOS period completes. Cancellation and sink precedence are retained. An additional unit test checks that a frame exceeding the remaining sample budget cannot change pending PCM or call the sink. This source revision still requires hosted GREEN compilation and tests; no local Rust build or model invocation was performed.

## Android shared-library identity repair

The hosted [Android component RED run 40337323631](https://github.com/Hatsunama/sign-to-speak/actions/runs/40337323631) checked exact source `09db33c28082d7305c91a6faaac355fb9a46fb55`. It compiled the actual ARM64 Rust C ABI library and JNI bridge, then failed the bridge ELF audit: `DT_NEEDED` named the Rust library by its absolute runner build path (`/home/runner/work/.../target/aarch64-linux-android/release/libsign_pocket_tts_runtime.so`) rather than `libsign_pocket_tts_runtime.so`. The Rust producer's ELF had no `DT_SONAME`; this is the observed link metadata defect. The failure does not establish a runtime, model, or device result.

`build.rs` now emits Cargo's cdylib-only linker argument for a stable `libsign_pocket_tts_runtime.so` SONAME on Linux and Android. For Android it also emits the 16 KiB maximum page size linker argument at the producer, alongside the existing hosted flag and ELF alignment audit. No dependency or model math changed. The hosted source manifest includes the build script, and the producer ELF audit requires the exact SONAME before the existing real JNI consumer link and `DT_NEEDED` audit. The focused policy tests guard both producer settings and both ELF audits. This candidate still needs a fresh hosted GREEN run; no local Rust/Android build or model/device test was performed.

These are control-flow and adapter-contract repairs. The RED failures do not establish that the pinned real model produces out-of-range samples, nonfinite samples, empty PCM, or an EOS failure. The component remains outside the app and has not been model-probed.

## Pinned English tokenizer byte fallback

The actual hosted component probe at [run 40337323556](https://github.com/Hatsunama/sign-to-speak/actions/runs/40337323556), job `121622284631`, checked source `09db33c28082d7305c91a6faaac355fb9a46fb55` and is **RED**: the real C ABI returned `Ok` (0) for `Hello ` followed by U+10FFFF and `.` where the probe required `Invalid` (2), before it reached the five positive utterances. The pinned tokenizer diagnostic showed `unknown_id=0`, preserved the noncharacter through normalization, and encoded it with byte fallback pieces including `<0xF4>` (ID 248), `<0x8F>` (147) and `<0xBF>` (195). CJK, emoji and U+200B likewise used byte fallback; ordinary `Café.` used a direct `é` piece (ID 745). The earlier general unknown-ID accessor was valid but did not address this failure: no unknown ID appeared in those fallback encodings.

The adapter now rejects exact SentencePiece `<0xHH>` pieces, retaining the unknown-ID check. This is the pinned English model's supported-text boundary: unsupported fallback text returns `Invalid` before any PCM; ordinary directly tokenized accents remain allowed. The mandatory real-model tokenizer diagnostic asserts the accent and unsupported examples, and the real C ABI probe checks noncharacter, CJK, emoji and zero-width cases without a PCM callback. Its five fixed positive utterances and callback, timing, and PCM checks remain required. Fake-ABI Python tests cover only probe transport expectations, not model behavior. A fresh hosted GREEN run is pending. Speech quality and Android/device behavior remain unproven.
